extra.message: User-supplied 'username' and 'password' arguments (from self.get_argument) are concatenated directly into the SQL string passed to cur.execute(). An attacker can inject SQL (e.g. username = admin'-- ) to bypass authentication or extract/modify data. Use parameterized queries instead.

The user-controlled 'server' POST argument is concatenated into a shell command string passed to os.popen('ping -c 3 ' + server). An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands (e.g. '127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd' or '$(rm -rf /)') leading to remote code execution. Avoid shell interpolation; use subprocess with a list of arguments and shell=False, and validate the input.

The 'file' GET argument is concatenated directly into a file path ('read/' + file_name) and opened for reading without sanitization. An attacker can supply '../../etc/passwd' (path traversal) to read arbitrary files on the server. Normalize and validate the path against a base directory.

The StaticHandler builds a file path from the unsanitized URL-captured 'path' ('static/' + path) and opens it for reading. Because the regex /static/(.*) captures arbitrary characters including '../', an attacker can traverse outside the static directory (e.g. /static/../server.py or /static/../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files. Validate the resolved path stays within the static base directory.

The 'q' GET argument is passed unescaped to search.html which renders it via {% raw query %} and inside an inline <script> via {% raw link %}. Combined with the explicitly disabled XSS filter (X-XSS-Protection: 0 set on line 88), this allows reflected Cross-Site Scripting. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript (e.g. </script><script>alert(1)</script> or ';alert(1);//). Use auto-escaping ({{ query }}) instead of {% raw %}.

The template outputs user-controlled values using {% raw query %} in the page body and {% raw link %} inside a <script> block, bypassing Tornado's auto-escaping. This directly enables reflected XSS via the 'q' search parameter. Replace {% raw %} with auto-escaped {{ }} expressions.

The handler explicitly sets the 'X-XSS-Protection' header to '0', disabling the browser's built-in reflected-XSS filter. This weakens defense-in-depth for the reflected XSS present on the search page.

The uploaded file's original filename is used to derive the extension (os.path.splitext) which is appended to the output path written to /tmp without sanitization. A crafted filename whose extension contains path traversal sequences (e.g. '.../../../some') influences the final written path. There is no authentication on the upload endpoint and no validation of file type/content, allowing arbitrary unauthenticated file writes to /tmp.

The UploadHandler.post (file upload), ContentHandler.get (arbitrary file read), and ServerHandler.post (command execution) endpoints have no authentication or authorization checks. Any unauthenticated remote user can upload files, read server files, and trigger OS command execution.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The Tornado Application is configured with 'debug': True. In production this enables verbose error tracebacks (which may leak source code, file paths, and stack traces to attackers) and auto-reload. Disable debug mode in production.

Hardcoded user credentials (including 'admin'/'admin' and several plaintext passwords) are embedded in source code and inserted into the database. Passwords are stored in plaintext (no hashing). This exposes credentials and reflects insecure credential management.

The login POST handler prints the full request body (which contains the username and plaintext password) to stdout/logs. ServerHandler.post (line 123) similarly logs request bodies. Logging sensitive credentials leads to sensitive data exposure in log files.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
